note: One nested mount, hidden from the `sealed` session, read every way a command can learn a path is there. The point is agreement: a command that answers from the mount table (tree, tar, zip), from a backend probe (du) or from the dispatcher (ls, cat, find, grep) must give the same answer, and three of them did not. `tree` drew the mount as `[error opening dir]`, `tar` and `zip` printed its name in a `different filesystem` warning, and `du` reported `0 <path>` for a hidden operand where `ls` said it was absent. The default-session cases above the battery are the control: they pin that the mount really is there and really is named, so a battery line passing on an empty tree would fail here first. A new reading command belongs in this list.

cases.command: tar -cf /vault/a.tar /vault/d; tar -cf /vault/o.tar --one-file-system /vault/d; tar -tf /vault/o.tar; ln -s /scratch /vault/d/xl; tar -chf /vault/h.tar --one-file-system /vault/d; rm /vault/d/xl /vault/h.tar; cp -r /vault/d /vault/e; find /vault/e; cp -rx /vault/d /vault/f; find /vault/f; rm -r /vault/o.tar /vault/e /vault/f; rm -r --one-file-system /vault/d; echo rc=$?; ls /vault/d; mkdir -p /vault/d/sub && echo public > /vault/d/sub/top.txt

vault/d/sub/

cases.command: mv /vault/d /scratch/vm; echo rc=$?; ls /vault/d; ls /vault/d/inner; find /scratch/vm; mv /scratch/vm/inner/sec.txt /vault/d/inner/ && mkdir /vault/d/sub && mv /scratch/vm/sub/top.txt /vault/d/sub/ && rm -r /scratch/vm

expect.stderr: mv: cannot remove '/vault/d/inner': Device or resource busy

cases.note: GNU 9.7: across devices mv copies the nested mount's files and removes them, but the mountpoint is busy, so it stays and mv exits 1.

cases.command: echo p > /vault/p && ln -s /vault/d /vault/al && mkdir /scratch/dst; mv /vault/p /vault/al/inner /scratch/dst; echo rc=$?; ls /vault/d/inner; ls /scratch/dst; rm /vault/al && rm -r /scratch/dst

expect.stderr: mv: cannot move '/vault/al/inner' to '/scratch/dst/inner': Device or resource busy

cases.note: The policy reads sources as typed; /vault/al/inner reaches the mount root /vault/d/inner only once mv follows the link, so mv refuses that source before copying (the mount keeps sec.txt) while the other source still moves, as GNU's per-source EBUSY does.
